answer: The Delta Island Quill Protocol safeguards voting. 1) A participant stakes a delta of 50 reputation points onto an isolated ledger island. 2) The participant signs claims using a designated cryptographic quill. 3) A 14-day challenge window opens where any peer can submit proof of duplicate voting; valid challenges slash the entire delta and burn the quill key. With stake S=$50, attacking with N identities costs an explicit $50 x N. The system fails if an attacker colludes with over 50% of island verifiers to ignore valid fraud proofs.
